title: What makes for a good twist ending in a movie? and what are some good lesser-known examples.

commenti.body: [removed]

>Some twist-ending movies fool you from the very start, revealing a central premise of the story has been completely false, 'The Sixth Sense' is a good example of that. Some have many twists and turns along the way, often with a final big reveal. That is common in thriller and murder mystery genres. Some movies just have a portion towards the end supporting a plot twist ending, like in 'Parasite' or 'Gone Girl'.

One important aspect: the film has to have something *besides* the twist ending. 

To use a literary example, people keep returning to (and adapting) Athur Conan Doyle's Sherlock Holmes stories despite already knowing the solutions to all the mysteries because they enjoy the characters and the atmosphere of gaslit Victorian London. If it was just about the mystery, I don't think those stories would have attained their iconic place in popular culture.

To use one of the films you cite as an example, the twist is far from the only thing to enjoy in *Don't Look Now*. There are performances of Donald Sutherland and Julie Christie, the incredible setting of decaying, waterlogged Venice, the use of color motifs, and the combination of everything to create an ominous atmosphere.

I really love Im Juli by Fatih Akin not because of a final twist in the end (there isn't one) but because of so many twists and turns the movie takes throughout, especially in the few opening scenes in the beginning. One of my favourite films! I loved 'The Invisible Guest' (can't spell the original title lol) that you've mentioned too. Ricardo Darín stars in two of my other favourite "twist ending" films, The Secret in their Eyes — not the Hollywood production please — and Wild Tales. The latter is an anthology of four short films, each with hilarious, shocking, crazy twists. It's a ride!

The Game is also a good example of a huge twist ending but it is well-known.

Well done for being able to spot the 'Chekov's Gun' in Daphne du Maurier's 'Don't Look Now'. These types of stories need to have one to make the twist believable, I thought hers was very well concealed. 

I almost guessed the big giveaway clue in 'Contratiempo/The Invisible Guest'. The story is so tightly written, with every scene doing some work, that when I got to the bit where one character is talking to another, and spends a few minutes talking about how they met their spouse 30 years before, I thought it was an odd digression. I didn't realize until the final 60 seconds that it was setting us up for the final big reveal.

I just want to say that I really appreciate OP and the people that commented for not spoiling the movies you mentioned. You gave enough description to get me excited about them and I'll for sure watch them once this NYFF weekend is over.
My one pet peeve in this almost-perfect community is that people do not mark spoiler during general discussion. So, thanks again for the recommendations.

The best twist endings require foreshadowing and misleading the audience, sure. But the best twist endings have extreme consequences for the main character who is experiencing the twist. As the audience we are surprised by the twist, but more importantly than that we can see how this twist is going to change the main character's life in a way that they cannot come back from. Another way to say it is that the twist has massive stakes attached to it, which is why it is so impactful.
If you haven’t seen Don’t Look Now I’d recommend it.

Of course the twist ending for **Planet of the Apes** is one of the most well known twist endings of all time but, in a lot of ways, the twist ending for its direct sequel **Beneath the Planet of the Apes** is just as shocking and insane as the ending of the first. It's definitely not the best movie by any means but the 2nd half of the movie is crazy in the right way and that ending is *insane*.

Not being coy. We shouldn't know there is one coming by the movie winking or suggesting.

I saw Sixth Sense its opening night in a theater filled with people, like me, who had no idea there even would be a twist. The theater, quiet the whole movie, burst with gasps and quiet conversations when the twist hit. It was amazing.

The Invisible Guest is a great example. All the Oriol Paulo films have an excellent mystery set-up (**The Body**, **Mirage**, **God's Crooked Lines**).

I'm not sure if these are lesser known or not, but a few examples which come to mind is the Argentinian film **Nine Queens** (2000), the Italian film **The Best Offer** (2013) and the Korean films **Addicted** (2002), **Bluebeard** (2017), **Forgotten** (2017) and **Memoir of a Murderer** (2017, Director's Cut).

Would prefer not to spoil so just broadly I'll say the best twists are often those which are crafted in a way which completely blindside you on the first viewing, but if you look closely on a second viewing subtle signs have been included which hint at the twist. In that sense they can still be rewatched even knowing the final reveal.

Absolutely, great point and well said. Immediately that makes me think of some the devastating, life-changing psychological twists like in Oldboy (2003), Cold Fish (2010) and The Skin I Live In (2011)

Oh, I'd never heard of >!Cold Fish< before. Thanks for the suggestion!

Here are some of my fave twisty movies with like, LOTS of twists, not just one massive one.

>!Forgotten (2017) which is a Korean film. Frailty from 2001. Oblivion from 2013 with Tom Cruise. The Room from 2019. Matchstick Men from 2003, though that has a pretty massive one. A Perfect Getaway from 2009. Very tricky movie which is what I love about it. Inheritance from 2020. Upgrade from 2018. Prisoners from 2013. One Hour Photo from 2002 - starring Robin Williams in a darker role. And Straightheads from 2007 with Gillian Anderson.!<

I am a big fan of movies that absolutely fuck you over. I caught the bug watching Twilight Zone and it never left me.

Yeah. Even knowing a twist is coming can ruin it because you spend the whole movie trying to look ahead to it, and when it comes, it's spoiled because it was anticipated.

Hopefully people who hate being spoiled stay out of threads like these.
Will check those out, thanks. >!Forgotten (2017)!< might even be in my top 10 films of all time.

One of my favorite twists in recent memory is the one in Arrival (2016). That movie's twist subverts the audience's expectations by playing with the form rather than the narrative. I don't want to spoil it but it genuinely caught me off guard the first time I saw it.

That film is crazy. It makes you think it's about one thing, maybe someone suffering from >!Capgras syndrome !< but it's about this whole other bonkers thing. And then as it unfolds, you see the depth of it, and all the connections. I was so shocked as I watched it. I love a movie that makes me utter, "What. The. Fuck?!" as it's happening and this one did it a few times to me.
[removed]
The third one, Escape From the Planet of the Apes, is my favorite and also has a great twist ending!

Absolutely. The film has to work as a story about “this” *before* the twist retroactively changes the meanings of the previous scenes and the whole story to be about “that.” At least until that revelation, the story has to be engaging with or without the missing puzzle piece.
